priorStories.headline: Riyadh airport closure extended through Saturday
priorStories.body:
Saudi aviation authorities extended the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport through 9 p.m. GMT on Saturday, October 17, following deadly attacks there over the weekend.

Saudi Arabia said it intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched toward Riyadh on Monday night. The Houthis said they targeted the airport with a ballistic missile and an airbase in southwestern Saudi Arabia with a drone, but Saudi authorities did not confirm any impacts from those claims.

priorStories.headline: Pacific storms kill five in Mexico
priorStories.body:
Mexican officials reported five deaths from Hurricane Simon and post-tropical cyclone Rachel, which brought flooding, landslides and infrastructure damage to the Pacific coast.

Four people died in Baja California, where six others remained missing, and another person died in a wall collapse in Guerrero. Mexico deployed 14,000 personnel in Baja California.

priorStories.headline: Hall and Woodford win economics Nobel
priorStories.body:
The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2026 economics prize to American economists Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford for research providing microeconomic foundations for macroeconomic stabilization.

Their models have influenced how governments and central banks respond to inflation, energy crises and other economic shocks.

candidates.summary: Eight people were injured in a stabbing at a supermarket in Incheon, South Korea, according to police and media reports. Initial reports said one person suffered cardiac arrest.
candidates.title: Eight injured in Incheon supermarket stabbing

candidates.summary: The Philippine Senate, sitting as an impeachment court, approved prosecutors' withdrawal of three charges against Vice President Sara Duterte. The action removed most of the charges in a trial that could affect Duterte's eligibility to run for president in 2028.
candidates.title: Philippine impeachment court drops most charges against Sara Duterte

candidates.summary: South Korea plans to move about 10,000 government jobs and 44 central government agencies from the Seoul metropolitan area to Sejong between 2027 and 2031, Yonhap reported.
candidates.title: South Korea plans transfer of 10,000 government jobs to Sejong

candidates.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned that an artificial-intelligence investment slowdown, rising sovereign bond yields or a major cyberattack could trigger broader financial instability. Its Global Financial Stability Report said banks remained broadly resilient in stress tests, though institutions representing 22% of global banking assets showed weak capital levels under the modeled downturn.
candidates.title: IMF warns of AI, bond and cyber risks to financial stability

candidates.summary: Asian stocks fell to their lowest level in more than two months as semiconductor shares sold off amid concerns about competition and the durability of the artificial-intelligence investment boom. South Korea's KOSPI dropped more than 6%, while Samsung fell 8%, SK Hynix 10% and Japan's Kioxia 14%.
candidates.title: Asian chip selloff pushes regional stocks to two-month low

candidates.summary: Ukrainian officials said Russian strikes overnight and Tuesday killed at least five people, including four in a destroyed Kharkiv apartment building, and wounded dozens. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said five ballistic missiles hit civilian infrastructure in Kyiv without advance warning from Ukraine's partners. Russia said it targeted military-industrial, logistics, railway and port facilities.
candidates.title: Russian strikes kill at least five across Ukraine

candidates.summary: France's finance minister said a cyberattack targeting connected refrigeration systems affected about 700 supermarkets. He told Parliament that the incident posed no risk to national food supplies, while the Paris prosecutor's office opened an investigation. The attack caused food losses and fires at some stores, and no group had publicly claimed responsibility.
candidates.title: France says supermarket cyberattack affected about 700 stores

candidates.summary: Pope Leo XIV was admitted to Rome's Gemelli hospital for planned surgery later Tuesday to remove a localized lung nodule. The procedure is intended to determine whether the lesion is malignant and whether further treatment is necessary. The Vatican canceled his audiences through October 20 and anticipated a hospital stay of about a week.
candidates.title: Pope Leo admitted for lung nodule surgery

candidates.summary: Formula 1 announced a 10-year agreement for Rwanda to host an African Grand Prix beginning in the early 2030s, after a purpose-built circuit is completed in Bugesera southeast of Kigali. The event would mark Formula 1's return to Africa for the first time since the 1993 South African Grand Prix.
candidates.title: Formula 1 announces African Grand Prix in Rwanda

candidates.summary: Polish officials accused Russian intelligence services of directing a September arson attack on Starlink infrastructure south of Warsaw. Two Turkish citizens arrested in Germany are accused of setting the fire. Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incident as hybrid warfare; Russia's response was not reported in the initial account.
candidates.title: Poland blames Russia for Starlink station arson

candidates.summary: Drones struck two commercial ships in the Black Sea near Bulgaria, sinking the Guinea-Bissau-flagged Dignity. Five sailors were rescued and 11 remained missing. All 15 crew members aboard the Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3 were evacuated, with five treated for minor injuries. Bulgarian authorities said responsibility had not been established; Ukrainian officials blamed Russia.
candidates.title: Drone strikes sink commercial ship off Bulgaria

candidates.summary: Pope Leo XIV underwent surgery that confirmed lung adenocarcinoma, and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung. The Vatican said the operation was successful and that decisions about chemotherapy or other treatment would await additional test results, including whether the cancer had spread to lymph nodes.
candidates.title: Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer after surgery

candidates.summary: Congo's Health Ministry reported 9,066 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,381 deaths, with 88 new cases in its latest report. The outbreak had spread across 65 health zones in seven provinces, and officials said many infections remained undetected while community transmission continued.
candidates.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak surpasses 9,000 confirmed cases

candidates.summary: The U.S. Treasury announced more than $1.21 billion in penalties against Bank of America for anti-money-laundering and sanctions violations. Treasury said the bank failed to report more than $5 billion in suspicious transactions on time. Bank of America admitted willfully violating the Bank Secrecy Act and said it was addressing the compliance failures.
candidates.title: US imposes more than $1.21 billion in penalties on Bank of America

candidates.summary: The Justice Department unsealed a complaint charging OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan with attempting to intercept oral communications using a concealed recording device in an executive conference room. The Saudi national was arrested October 9 and appeared in federal court Tuesday. The complaint's allegations have not been proven in court.
candidates.title: OpenAI employee charged over hidden recording device

candidates.summary: The U.S. Justice Department announced charges against 14 people and the arrests of two Americans accused of supporting North Korean remote-worker schemes. Authorities said operations targeting more than 40 suspected Texas "laptop farms" seized approximately 187 devices. The alleged schemes affected more than 70 U.S. companies and generated at least $3 million for overseas workers.
candidates.title: US announces crackdown on North Korean remote-worker schemes

candidates.summary: AT&T agreed to sell its Mexican wireless business to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings for $2 billion in cash, subject to adjustments and regulatory approval. The companies expect the transaction to close in the first quarter of 2027; AT&T said the pending divestiture would sharpen its focus on U.S. fiber and 5G investment.
candidates.title: AT&T agrees to sell Mexico unit for $2 billion

candidates.summary: The death toll from Hurricane Simon and the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel rose to six after authorities reported another body found near a stream in Baja California on Tuesday. Five people remained missing in the state. Simon strengthened while moving parallel to Mexico's Pacific coast, bringing additional flooding risks.
candidates.title: Mexico storm death toll rises to six

candidates.summary: Islamic State West Africa Province militants attacked a military base in Kukawa, Borno state, on Tuesday. Nigeria's military said an unspecified number of soldiers were killed and more than 25 militants died in a counteroffensive. A military officer who was not authorized to speak publicly told the Associated Press that 10 soldiers were killed.
candidates.title: Islamic State-affiliated militants attack Nigerian military base

candidates.summary: CVS agreed to pay $315 million to resolve U.S. government allegations that it filled unlawful prescriptions for opioids and other controlled substances and sought federal reimbursement for some prescriptions. CVS also entered an agreement requiring measures including monitoring dispensing patterns and establishing a reporting hotline. The settlement resolves allegations without a determination of liability.
candidates.title: CVS agrees to $315 million opioid-prescription settlement

candidates.summary: The U.S. Treasury sanctioned four individuals and 11 entities that it said were connected to Mexico's Cartel del Noreste. The designations targeted alleged cartel-linked operations in horse racing, construction, trucking, and the oil and gas sector, including the Club La Molienda racetrack near Nuevo Laredo.
candidates.title: US sanctions Cartel del Noreste commercial network

candidates.summary: The U.S. Justice Department announced results from a coordinated operation targeting online scam networks in West Africa. Authorities made 28 arrests in Ghana and Nigeria, while private companies removed more than 3.7 million accounts, pages and groups. Officials said 117 suspected trafficking victims were identified in Ghana pending repatriation to Nigeria, and more than $11 million in potentially freezable funds was identified.
candidates.title: International operation disrupts West African scam networks

candidates.summary: The United States recalled its chargé d’affaires in Nicaragua for consultations after Nicaragua rejected the Trump administration's nominee for U.S. ambassador. The State Department said Managua's denial of diplomatic approval showed an unwillingness to engage in productive dialogue.
candidates.title: US recalls top envoy to Nicaragua after ambassador nominee rejected
